note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 2e4be94ae3). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 9.3.1: "A decimal64 value is lexically represented as an optional sign ("+" or "-"), followed by a sequence of decimal digits, optionally followed by a period ('.') as a decimal indicator and a sequence of decimal digits." The units changed only from validateYangType to ValidateType, which is the same producer path (validateLeafValue with no leaf). validateDecimal64 tests ^[+-]?\d+(\.\d+)?$ (ASCII digits in Go RE2) before the fraction-digits parse. Positive accepts +1.5, -1.5, -10.5, 1, 0.25, 0.0, 10.50; negative refuses .5, 1., +, -, 1.2.3, abc and the empty string with ErrTypeType and 'expected decimal64', with fraction-digits and range refusals asserted as distinct kinds. Each clause of the sentence has a value that would flip if the regexp lost it; records on validateDecimal64 replay.
